spans.s:
pánthan [433], m. road, path, way. [cf.
πἀτος, ‘path’; Lat. pont-em, ‘path, bridge’:
Eng. path and Ger. Pfad, if they belong
here at all, must be regarded as very early
borrowings, fr. the Greek πάτος, or poss.
from the Scythian.]

pā́na,
 —1. n. the drinking (esp. of strong
drink);
 —2. perhaps as vbl adj. drenching,
 i. e. tränkend. [√1pā, ‘drink,’
1150.]

pānīya-varṣa, m. water-rain, downpour
of water.
